Inherited red-cell dehydration and hemolysis; gallstones are separately diagnosed, ferritin alone does not prove liver damage, and pseudohyperkalemia is an artifact.
Intellectual disability, callosal agenesis, microphthalmia and orofacial clefting define the syndrome; defining heminasal hypoplasia supports the pulmonary axis.
Sulfation-related metabolic skeletal dysplasia; cleft palate in 4/4 and hearing impairment in 4/7 support gastrointestinal and otologic involvement.
Primary endometrial carcinoma; reproductive organs have no axis.
Defined by endocardial inflammation; the umbrella includes infective and sterile forms without a shared infectious or autoimmune mechanism.
Radial-ray defects, ocular motor dysfunction and hearing loss define the syndrome; thrombocytopenia affects 13/21 (~62%).
Congenital skeletal malformations of the hands and feet; no established extra-skeletal organ damage.
Immunodeficiency and microcephaly define NBS; supplied HPO reports cytopenias and anorectal defects at 80-99%, although these frequency estimates are atypical.
Androgenetic hair-follicle miniaturization and alopecia; androgen sensitivity does not establish endocrine gland disease.
Mucin deposition in skin and its appendages; systemic involvement is not shared across this heterogeneous umbrella.
Defined by cardiac conduction disease and congenital phalangeal abnormalities.
Immune dysregulation with lymphoproliferation and multilineage cytopenias; hepatomegaly alone does not establish hepatic damage, and hepatitis is under 30%.
Ovarian teratoma containing thyroid tissue; reproductive origin has no axis, and functional thyrotoxicosis occurs in a minority.
Meconium directly obstructs and inflames neonatal lungs; pulmonary hypertension is occasional and encephalopathy very rare.
Congenital unilateral destruction or absence of cerebral cortex; presumed prenatal vascular disruption does not establish systemic vascular disease.
Chronic cutaneous collagen degeneration with granulomatous inflammation, atrophy and ulceration; associated diabetes is a separate disease.
Bleeding occupies and can damage a joint; hemarthrosis itself does not establish an underlying coagulation disorder.
Primary breast carcinoma with salivary-type histology; breast has no axis, and histologic resemblance does not imply salivary gland involvement.
Benign cutaneous proliferation of keratinocytes and melanocytes.
Progressive spastic paraplegia, intellectual disability and glaucoma define the syndrome; each is reported at 80-99%.
Juvenile iron overload with hypogonadism and hepatic fibrosis/cirrhosis (2/2); iron cardiomyopathy affects roughly 30-50% of juvenile cases. Pigmentation alone adds no skin damage.
Active mycobacterial infection; direct pulmonary infection and tissue injury occur in approximately 80% of cases, while extrapulmonary sites vary.
Complex I deficiency with lactic acidosis; cardiomyopathy, callosal dysplasia and anemia each occur in the single reported patient (1/1); population frequencies remain uncertain.
Defined by relapsing facial neuropathy, granulomatous orofacial inflammation and tongue abnormalities; skin inflammation and cheilitis occur at 80-99%.
